changes: KnowledgeBaseEditor merges five independent form states into one draft and shares the GET/POST/PUT request state and receipt validation. It reuses apiJson for existing authentication, desktop proof, dynamic backend origin and bounded cancellation.

The editor is owned by account, role, work domain, organization and article ID. Strict remounts and scope changes cancel obsolete requests. A failed initial read offers explicit retry instead of an editable empty record. Failed saves retain input; duplicate writes are blocked and form fields are disabled until confirmation.

Only a valid article receipt may update the draft, publish the existing knowledge-updated event and call onSaved. Creation clears the draft while retaining its category. The unmanaged 350 ms navigation timer, duplicate success/error markup and duplicate tag-array formatting were deleted.

TokenDashboard combines initial loading, polling and manual refresh under one request lifecycle and one state object. Polling schedules the next read 10 seconds after the previous one settles, with a 15 second request timeout. Account or time-range changes cancel old reads and clear their displayed data.

Usage requests reuse apiJson and validate rendering-critical result fields. Failed refreshes clear stale data and display an error; automatic and manual retry remain available. Provider labels and colors share one map, and both the ring and provider list reuse one segment calculation. Unused view-only payload fields and a one-call number-format wrapper were removed; locale updates remain subscribed.
validationNotes: Four new behavior tests mount the actual editor and usage dashboard against synthetic fetch: confirmed creates, denied and malformed receipts, normalization, duplicate clicks, desktop proof, retained failed edits, obsolete reads/saves, StrictMode, article/organization/account transitions, logout, failed-load retry, sequential polling, failed-refresh recovery and timer cleanup.
The polling test advances a synthetic scheduler. It proves no interval overlap, recovery and cleanup; it does not benchmark production latency or simulate the native AbortSignal timeout clock.

13 focused files passed without skipped tests. Lint includes TypeScript and hook/i18n boundaries; all-frontend and desktop builds plus compact-layout checks passed. Earlier prune40-69 latest source baselines and final fingerprints were checked.
An initial TypeScript check caught lost string narrowing in the tag parser. Retaining the raw string fixed it before final verification.
limitations: Frontend cancellation cannot undo an article write already accepted by the server. This batch does not alter backend persistence or prove that asynchronous knowledge indexing has completed; existing article response semantics remain unchanged.

Usage ownership remains per user across organizations, matching the existing backend. Polling waits after settlement rather than maintaining a fixed wall-clock cadence; response checks cover rendered fields rather than the full data schema.

No production API/model calls, user-record edits, native client acceptance, full-suite run, backend rebuild, commit, push, deployment or client restart were performed. This batch does not certify whole-project simplification complete.
remainingCandidates: OrgMembers still has separate load/invite/delete request state and lacks scoped cancellation; member.id and userId differ, so direct collection-hook substitution needs contract review.
GitHubMCPBrowser search results can arrive after switching sources and errors are displayed like empty results; inspect cancellation and failure handling before merging renderers.
BusinessWorkbench has independently managed reads, binding/import operations and artifact cache lifetimes; no change was made to those flows in this batch.
